We need to propose a retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <= $9999 (we cannot check price but assume typical). Need to produce JSON route.

We need to find suitable templates. Use search with proper list.

We need to break the target into fragments. The target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

It is a sulfonamide linking a tolyl sulfonyl group to a phenyl-alkenyl-amide-aniline.

Potential disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give tolyl sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and aniline derivative (the rest). So precursor 1: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl chloride) and precursor 2: aniline with the rest (maybe 4-((E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide) phenyl). Actually the rest is an aniline attached to amide: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the sulfonamide attaches to an aniline (the phenyl ring c2...). So we could have 4-((E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide) phenyl sulfonyl chloride reacting with p-toluidine? Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to the tolyl ring (para methyl). The N is attached to the sulfonyl group and to the phenyl ring (c2...). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (c2...). So the sulfonyl chloride would be p-tolylsulfonyl chloride reacting with the aniline (the phenyl ring with amide side chain). So precursor A: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (commercial). Precursor B: 4-((E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide) phenyl (i.e., an aniline bearing the side chain). That aniline could be made via amide formation between acryloyl chloride and 4-aminophenyl? Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Wait the side chain: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So it's an amide linking a phenyl-amine (aniline) to a cinnamoyl group (E-CH=CH-CO-). So the phenyl ring c3ccccc3N is an aniline (para? not specified). So the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (c3...). So the amide is formed between acryloyl chloride (or acryloyl acid) and 4-aminophenyl? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (c3ccccc3N) which has an NH2 substituent? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with an NH attached to carbonyl (amide) and also an NH2 on the ring? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N" means an aniline where the nitrogen attached to carbonyl is attached to the aromatic carbon (i.e., anilide) and there is also an NH attached to the aromatic carbon? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is ambiguous: The first N is attached to carbonyl (C(=O)N...), then "c3ccccc3N" means the aromatic ring with an N attached at the end (an aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (forming anilide) and the ring also has an NH2 substituent (para? unspecified). So the amide is anilide of 4-aminobenzamide? Actually it's 4-aminobenzamide? Wait typical SMILES for p-aminobenzamide is "Nc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)N". Here we have "C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N" which is an amide where the nitrogen is attached to phenyl ring (anilide) and the phenyl ring has an NH2 substituent (maybe para). So it's 4-aminobenzamide (para-aminobenzamide) but the carbonyl is attached to the nitrogen, not to the ring. So it's 4-aminobenzamide (para-aminobenzamide) but the carbonyl is attached to the nitrogen (makes sense). So the side chain is cinnamoyl attached to 4-aminobenzamide? Actually the carbonyl is attached to the nitrogen which is attached to phenyl ring with NH2. So the amide is formed between cinnamoyl chloride and 4-aminobenzenamine (p-phenylenediamine). So precursor B could be p-phenylenediamine (commercial) plus cinnamoyl chloride (commercial) to form the amide.

Thus overall route:

Step 1: Form amide: React p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene) with cinnamoyl chloride (or acryloyl chloride? Actually need CH=CH-CO-). Cinnamoyl chloride (ClC(=O)C=CC) is commercially available? Possibly. Or we could use cinnamic acid + coupling reagent. But we can assume cinnamoyl chloride is available.

Result: 4-((E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide) (i.e., aniline with amide side chain). This product still has an NH2 on the ring (the other amine). That's the aniline that will later react with sulfonyl chloride.

Step 2: Sulfonylation: React the aniline (product from step1) with p-tolylsulfonyl chloride to give the target sulfonamide.

Thus total 2 steps.

Leaves: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride, p-phenylenediamine, cinnamoyl chloride. All commercially available and cheap.

We need to verify templates: need sulfonyl chloride reacting with aniline (sulfonamide formation). Template likely exists. Also amide formation between acid chloride and amine.

We should check template IDs via search. Let's search for amide formation (functional_groups_broken: amine, functional_groups_formed: amide).
